source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Rear Suspension and Drive Line, p.4-37

procedures.title: Propeller shaft (Dana): remove, repair and install
steps: (continued) Repairs: remove the bearing lock rings from the trunnion yoke.
Set the yoke on a length of 1-1/4" I.D. pipe on the press bed.
Press the trunnion down with a socket or rod far enough to push the bearing cup out of the yoke (see figure 94 in the manual).
Take the dust seals off; clean and inspect rollers and trunnion; repack the bearings with lithium-base chassis lubricant.
Fit new dust seals with the cavity toward the trunnion end; set J-21548 over the trunnion end into the seal cavity and press until it bottoms on the trunnion (see figure 95 in the manual).
Start one cup into the yoke, set the trunnion into it, add the other cup and press both in, keeping the trunnion aligned (see figure 96 in the manual).
Press the cups far enough to fit the lock rings, and fit them.
Installation: check the yoke seal in the transmission and replace it if needed (see the transmission section).

Slide the front yoke into the transmission. On Corvettes, fit the front yoke into the transmission, then place the shaft between that yoke and the companion flange and fit the U-bolts at the front yoke.
Line the shaft up with the companion flange using the removal marks and connect the rear U-joint with the U-bolt clamps over the trunnion bearings; torque the nuts to specification carefully.
notes: Because the shaft is long, a bench vise may be handier than an arbor press; the steps are the same.
Fill the grease reservoir at each trunnion end fully, packing from the bottom (a squeeze bottle is recommended) to avoid air pockets.
Seal fitting is critical: use the specified tool so the seal does not distort and seats properly.
Over-tightening the U-bolt nuts can cause early bearing failure.
